scope: Implement the local 7BH.3 canonical batch output suffix and filesystem-identity protection without adding test drawings; record a separately observed future-name collation gap.

changes.details: Batch output filenames replace the input extension with .dxf before collision preflight and conversion. Existing lexical and filesystem-identity protections remain; native future-name collation is not implemented.

Batch expectations use the canonical .dxf suffix; the focused batch selector verifies an existing repository AC1015 DWG produces ASCII DXF under .dxf, reopens through normal suffix dispatch, rejects same-stem DWG/DXF inputs in both list orders, and refuses temporary symlink/hard-link output aliases before publication. A separate unretained reproducer observed that case-equivalent future names bypass lexical preflight on the local case-insensitive volume.

Updated PAR-103, 7BH status, next-action notes, and implementation progress. A future-name collation gap is recorded, while implementation remains deferred until native capability and comparison semantics are established.

caseEquivalentFutureOutputReproduction.observed: Lexical preflight returned success and both normalized output names referred to the same filesystem name.
caseEquivalentFutureOutputReproduction.expectedSafeBehavior: Reject the batch before conversion and leave the output directory unchanged.

remaining: Implement collision detection using verified filesystem-native capabilities and name-equivalence semantics; do not substitute ASCII folding or a small set of probes.
Qualify case-equivalent output collision behavior on native Linux and Windows, including per-directory case settings, normalization, platform aliases, and failure/cleanup behavior.
Review whether identity indexing can be optimized without weakening the preflight contract.
